specific_prose_corrections: A four-cell path names node order and every edge pair before matrix rows, degree entries, six pair distances and BFS layers are used.
The regular ring hand example counts 60 edges and clustering 3/6. Traversal records select the retained endpoint; sorting an undirected edge is only its storage representation.
Each exchange edge contributes equal/opposite flow and a four-entry matrix block. Normalized k in 1/T and physical g in V/T connect through the common volume.
The disconnected four-node solution expands constant and difference modes. A quadratic edge identity explains nonnegative eigenvalues and one zero mode per component.
Unequal-volume equilibrium follows from common concentration and component amount. Euler coefficients give the positive-weight-node bound; isolated nodes remain outside the minimum.
SIR tables name time, receiver and old infected-neighbor indices. Two updates explicitly separate newly infected individuals from old individuals recovering during the same update.

The nested table example gives within 1, between 4, overall 4 and total variance 5. Finite graph means contain propagation sampling variation; the experiment also rotates starts and records a fixed 12-step cumulative outcome.
The printed size-one proportion describes no newly infected individual during observation. It is not automatically an extinction rate; plots show graph means/differences rather than this proportion.
Unit-circle vectors explain R, antiphase clusters and common rotation. Frequency uses unwrapped displacement and a specified window rather than endpoint phase concentration.
The synchrony scan uses four frequency assignments times four initial phases, standard-deviation bars, a 4 T tail window and an endpoint-R step comparison.
The capstone uses the actual four-node ring, with degree sum 8, mean path 4/3, first exchange state [3.6,0.2,0,0.2] and initial R about 0.4742.
The browser diffusion holds 80 update steps: changing h also changes observation length. The web synchrony tail is 60×0.035=2.1 T; sliders and numerical models are unchanged.
The invisible third-example reference in the one-phase-step question was replaced with the visible sample and a general isolated-node rule.
